title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 9
paragraphs: At last, however, the answer was given and the Spartans' departure came about in the following way. On the day before the one appointed for the last hearing of the envoys, Chileos of Tegea — who of all foreigners had the greatest influence in Lacedaemon — heard from the Ephors all that the Athenians were saying; and he, it seems, said to them these words: “This is how matters stand, Ephors: if the Athenians are not friendly to us but become allies of the barbarian, then though a strong wall may have been built across the Isthmus, a wide gate has been opened for the Persian into the Peloponnese. Listen to their request, before the Athenians resolve on something else tending to the fall of Greece.”
